acceptanceCriteria.notes: Two halves, and the second is what makes the first mean anything: a stored status field could produce the same display and go stale silently. Pass/fail without judgement — the stage either changes or it does not, and the field either exists or it does not.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With the application running, changing a recorded attestation so that a different stage becomes the earliest unready one causes the project view to display that stage as current, without restarting the application. No field storing a stage or status value exists anywhere under the content root.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The displayed current stage follows the attestations on disk

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NO PARTIAL-FAILURE EXCEPTION, deliberately. AST-0035 measured the skeleton printing 178 while rendering 177 — the count is what turns an incomplete page into a misleading one, because an operator reading the total has been told the missing thing is present. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27, AND THE ORIGINAL WAS NOT MERELY IMPRECISE — IT WAS UNFALSIFIABLE. It asked that each displayed total equal 'the number rendered on the page'. The project view renders TOTALS, not artifact entries, so there is nothing on the page to count: the criterion compared a number with itself and would have passed on any implementation, including one that printed a constant. ⚠️ The fix is an INDEPENDENT ORACLE. A fixture with known composition is the only source of truth the application cannot influence, which is what makes this a test rather than a tautology. It is the same defect as a check nobody has seen fail (ACC-0024), reached from the other direction: there, the check had never been shown to fail; here, it could not.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Evaluated against a fixture content root whose composition is known in advance. For each artifact type, the total the project view displays equals the number of files of that type in the fixture that parse successfully and validate. Ground truth comes from the fixture, not from the page: the count is computed independently of the application and compared with what was rendered.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every displayed total equals the fixture's parsable artifacts of that type

acceptanceCriteria.notes: All three clauses are required together. Naming the file without correcting the count still leaves the page asserting an artifact it did not render; correcting the count without naming the file leaves an operator hunting for what changed.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With exactly one artifact file under the content root made unparseable, the project view (a) names that file's path, (b) shows a parse position, and (c) prints a total for that type exactly one lower than before. The response is not an error page: every other artifact still renders.
acceptanceCriteria.title: An unreadable artifact is named, located, and subtracted from its count

acceptanceCriteria.notes: This is the clause that stops a page-level boundary satisfying DEC-0019 on paper. One boundary wrapping everything makes the whole page the fallback, which technically has a loading state and buys nothing.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The initial HTML of the stage view contains a distinct loading fallback for the exit-criteria region and for the stage-document region. Delaying either read leaves the other region's content rendered and only its own fallback showing.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The stage view's reads resolve behind separate boundaries

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The negative criteria above are satisfiable by a compiler that refuses everything. This is the control that stops that.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A stage document containing markdown and only components from the permitted set compiles, renders its markdown structure, and renders each permitted component it uses.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A permitted document renders, including its mapped components

acceptanceCriteria.notes: AST-0034 measured the skeleton's idle and dead streams as byte-identical, which is the strongest possible form of indistinguishable. 'Not by colour alone' keeps the fix legible to anyone who cannot rely on a colour difference.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: When heartbeats stop arriving, the page shows a stale indication that is distinguishable from the healthy state by text or icon and not by colour alone, within the configured watchdog window.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A stopped heartbeat produces a visibly stale page within the watchdog window

acceptanceCriteria.notes: AST-0034 measured the gap being lost with nothing to recover it from. The last sentence records the design that makes this cheap: because events are hints and never deltas, a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: After the stream drops and reconnects, the client reloads, and a content change made during the disconnected window is reflected in what the page then shows. No event buffer, event id or `Last-Event-ID` handling is required to achieve this.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Reconnection reloads, and a change made while disconnected is then visible

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ SCOPED TO CORRECTNESS-CRITICAL STATE, per DEC-0023's corrected wording. Transient interface state is permitted and is not covered here. The reason this needs a criterion at all is that DEC-0022 reloads the page on every content change and every reconnection — at a moment the user did not choose, and without telling them what was lost.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: For each selection the views expose that is not purely presentational — at minimum the selected stage and the selected artifact — opening the same URL in a session with no prior client storage restores the same selection.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every correctness-critical selection survives a reload in a fresh session

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ WRITTEN FROM A MEASUREMENT, not from caution. AST-0039 recorded what production actually does when the compiler refuses a document inside a `<Suspense>` boundary: HTTP 200, because the shell has already streamed, and a React error digest with no message, no path and no position. The compiler's diagnostic is exact and reaches only the server log. ⚠️ 200 IS NOT THE DEFECT AND IS EXPLICITLY ACCEPTED. Streaming means the status is committed before the failure is known, and demanding a 5xx would mean giving up streaming for a document the operator can be told about in place. What is refused is INVISIBILITY — a blank region and a success status for a document the compiler rejected precisely. ⚠️ THE ESCAPING CLAUSE IS NOT HOUSEKEEPING. The diagnostic quotes the offending source, which is agent-authored content; rendering it as markup would let a refused document inject into the page that reports its refusal — turning the safety mechanism into the delivery route. ⚠️ 'The rest of the page still renders' is what makes this a criterion about ONE region rather than about error handling in general: the exit criteria live behind their own boundary and a refused document must not take them down with it.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: When the restricted compiler refuses a stage document, the served page renders an error inside the document region that (a) is visible in the response body, (b) names the document by a REPOSITORY-RELATIVE path, (c) carries a line and column, and (d) has its diagnostic text HTML-escaped rather than interpolated as markup. The stage's exit criteria and the rest of the page still render. A partial page returning HTTP 200 satisfies this criterion; a response whose document region contains only an opaque error digest, or nothing at all, FAILS it.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A refused stage document fails VISIBLY, in the document region, with a location

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The endpoint returns exactly the keys service, protocol, runId, projectId and build — no more and no fewer, as a set rather than in a fixed order — with the service name and the versioned protocol fixed, the run and project identifiers equal to the ones supplied to this process, and the build version read from the package the running code was loaded from rather than from the environment, which could only ever match itself. A response carrying an additional key, missing a key, or carrying the two identifiers exchanged, fails; asserting only the absence of known sensitive patterns does not satisfy this, because it passes on every field nobody thought to pattern-match. Every field of a successful response is built from a validated value: both identifiers must be strings matching the fixed 32-character lowercase hexadecimal format, and the build version must match a character set containing no path separator, colon or whitespace. Nothing that fails those checks is echoed, so the absence of any absolute path, credential, session content or planning content holds by construction across the whole response rather than by scanning the output. An identity that is not whole is not an identity: a missing, unreadable or unsafe build version answers 503 exactly as a missing run identity does, never a 200 with a null field. Each failure answers with its own exact key set and a distinguishing error, never a 200 with fields missing and never an invented identifier. The status, headers and parsed body are observed over real HTTP for both the identified and the unidentified case, and the served identity is proved to come from the running process rather than the build by starting the application with an identity different from the one present when it was built.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The health response is exactly an identity, asserted field by field

accepted.notes: ⚠️ The count rule admits no partial-failure exception. AST-0035 measured the skeleton printing 178 while rendering 177: the total is what turns an incomplete page into a misleading one. ⚠️ SPLIT 2026-08-27 — it was named as visibly oversized when the plan was written, and it was. The totals, the lint surface and located parse failures are its sibling. This half is the navigation spine; that half is the truthfulness rules, and they fail in different ways. ⚠️ Depends on BOTH boundary checks, so every view file written from here on is checked as it lands. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28, and it is the first task whose code the boundary checks actually guard. Before it the lint reported `0 reader consumer(s)` and the two `<Suspense>` detectors had nothing in the real project to examine; it now reports 1 consumer and 6 reachable modules, and both detectors were falsified against `app/page.js` itself. ⚠️ VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION, NOT INFERRED: with `next start` running and nothing rebuilt, changing one attestation on disk moved the displayed current stage from none to `04-requirement-gaps`, and reverting the file moved it back. ⚠️ The smoke check now asserts the READING PANEL's markers as well as the route's. Without that a page whose Suspense boundary never resolved would still pass — the shell ships, the fallback ships, and the content never arrives, which is the streaming form of a build that succeeds while rendering nothing.
accepted.statement: Render `/`: the current stage derived from stage definitions and recorded attestations, and all nine stages with their gate state. Status is conveyed by text or icon, never by colour alone. No stored status field is introduced anywhere.
accepted.title: Build the project view's stage navigation and derived current stage

accepted.notes: At most one stage document per render: DEC-0020's per-request compilation cost is unmeasured, and a view rendering several would multiply an unknown. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. The smoke check now covers `/stage/[stageId]` and requires every region to RESOLVE — criteria, criterion rows, document and review — then rewrites the document in the copy twice: once with a permitted component, asserting it renders, and once with an unmapped one, asserting a located and escaped refusal beside intact criteria. Falsified by removing the catch: the rejection escapes, the region goes blank, and the check fails. ⚠️ ONE THING IS MEASURED AND NOT FIXABLE HERE: an unknown stage returns 200, not 404. `notFound()` runs inside a Suspense child, so the status is committed before the stage turns out not to exist. Validating earlier means reading in the route entry, which the boundary check refuses — so the honest position is that the failure is VISIBLE (Next.js's not-found UI) while the status is not available to make truthful. Recorded as an omission rather than quietly accepted.
accepted.statement: Render `/stage/[stageId]`: the stage's exit criteria with their recorded attestations, then the compiled document, then a review panel identifying the artifact under review by id, type, title and current status. Long criterion identifiers wrap rather than overflow.
accepted.title: Build the stage view: criteria above the document, artifact-scoped review

accepted.notes: ⚠️ Needed because DEC-0022 reloads the page on every content change and every reconnection — at a moment the user did not choose, and without telling them what was lost. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28, and most of the mechanism arrived with TSK-0009 — the stage id is a route segment and the artifact id a query parameter, both read server-side and neither turned into a path. What this task added is the PROOF: fresh-session, reload and control fetches, an invalid-id case, and static checks that no application module reaches for browser storage and no client component holds a selection. ⚠️ THE STATIC CHECKS PASS TRIVIALLY TODAY because there are no client components at all. They are written anyway: the first `"use client"` file is exactly when someone reaches for `useState` to remember which artifact is open, and that is the moment this should fail rather than the moment someone notices a reload lost their place. The count of client components is pinned so it moving is a visible event. ⚠️ DEC-0024 records the accepted 200-for-an-unknown-stage tradeoff, with the reopening condition being a consumer that parses the response rather than reads it.
accepted.statement: Encode the selected stage and the selected artifact in the URL so that opening it in a session with no prior client storage restores the same selection. Transient interface state may remain in the client.
accepted.title: Put every correctness-critical selection in the URL

accepted.notes: ⚠️ Split from TSK-0007 on 2026-08-27, because the truthfulness rules are where this view fails SILENTLY and they deserve their own review rather than riding along with the navigation. ⚠️ THE COUNT RULE ADMITS NO PARTIAL-FAILURE EXCEPTION. AST-0035 measured the skeleton printing 178 while rendering 177: the total is what turns an incomplete page into a misleading one, because an operator reading it has been told the missing thing is present. ⚠️ ACC-0014 is evaluated against a FIXTURE of known composition, never against the page — the page renders totals rather than entries, so counting what it shows would compare a number with itself. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Nine tests: an offline fixture with a declared composition, a corrupt-one case, a control proving a file count and a parsed count genuinely differ, static checks that the panel re-judges nothing, and a production sequence that corrupts a file while serving, requires the total to fall by one and the located error to appear, then restores it and requires both to recover — with no rebuild and no restart. ⚠️ FALSIFIED WITH A CONSTANT TOTAL AND WITH SUPPRESSED ERROR OUTPUT, as required, and each failed only its own assertion. That separation is the point: a single check covering both would let a page that counts correctly but hides failures pass on the strength of its arithmetic. ⚠️ THE READER HAD THE SAME DEFECT THE SKELETON DID. `artifactCount` was `lint.records.length` — a FILE count — since TSK-0005. It was never displayed, so nothing had caught it; writing the component that would have displayed it is what did.
accepted.statement: Add to `/`: artifact totals for each type, lint findings surfaced rather than re-judged, and reporting for a file that fails to parse — named with its path and a position, omitted from the page, and subtracted from its type's total. No rendered total may include an artifact the page did not render.
accepted.title: Build the project view's artifact totals, lint surface and located parse failures

accepted.notes: ⚠️ Split from TSK-0011 on 2026-08-27. This is the half REQ-0018's second clause actually lands on. AST-0034 measured the skeleton's idle and dead streams as byte-identical and no client-side cleverness recovers a difference that was never transmitted — but equally, a heartbeat nothing listens for is not visibility either, so neither half is sufficient alone. ⚠️ Reload on reconnection is what removes the work: events are hints and never deltas (#73), so a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up and no replay machinery is needed. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Thirteen deterministic tests plus a production check that the client half actually reaches the browser. ⚠️ ACC-0029 AND ACC-0030 REMAIN NOT-EVALUATED, DELIBERATELY. No browser was available, so a visibly stale page within the watchdog window and a reconnection that recovers a missed change have not been seen happening. They are the two criteria a reasonable person would most want ticked, which is precisely why they are not. ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY CHECK RELOCATED THE CODE. `lib/stream-watchdog.mjs` was refused by `lint:shell` on its first run; `app/server/*` was impossible because `server-only` throws in a client component. `app/_stream/logic.js` is neither tool nor adapter, which is what a client component needs — the same shape `app/_mdx/reject-js.js` already had. ⚠️ THE SMOKE CHECK LOOKS PAST THE HTML. Server-rendered markup for a client component is identical whether or not the script ships, so the check fetches every script the page loads and requires one to contain the component's own text. Falsified with a static stand-in that passes the markup assertions and fails only that one.
accepted.statement: Subscribe to the stream, listen for the named heartbeat event, and run a watchdog that renders a visibly stale state — by text or icon, not colour alone — when a heartbeat does not arrive within its window. Reload on a change hint and on reconnection. No event buffer, event id or `Last-Event-ID` handling.
accepted.title: Build the change-stream client: listener, watchdog, stale state, reload on reconnect

accepted.statement: Add the Kiln health endpoint to the application, taking the run and project identifiers supplied by the supervisor at start, and returning only the identity fields.
accepted.title: Add the run-identity health route

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ DERIVED, NEVER STORED (#16). Stage position is computed from definitions plus attestations on every read; there is no status field to go stale. ⚠️ THE TRUTHFUL-COUNT RULE IS THIS COMPONENT'S SHARPEST CONSTRAINT and it comes from a measured defect: AST-0035 found the skeleton reporting 178 artifacts while rendering 177, because a malformed file vanished and the total did not move. A count is a claim, and a claim about content that was not rendered is false. No partial-failure exception. ⚠️ OUTSIDE ITS BOUNDARY: it surfaces lint findings, it does not re-judge them (#47). ⚠️ HALF BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0007: the derived current stage and all nine stages with their gate state. ACC-0013 passes, measured in production. ⚠️ ACC-0014, ACC-0015 AND ACC-0035 REMAIN `not-evaluated`. Counts, the lint surface and located parse failures are TSK-0016's, and URL-recoverable selection is TSK-0010's. The split was made because this half fails VISIBLY — a wrong stage is obvious — while the counting half fails silently, and they deserve separate review. ⚠️ THE READ LIVES IN `<StagesPanel />`, RENDERED LITERALLY INSIDE A `<Suspense>` AT THE PAGE'S OWN CALL SITE, and that form is now enforced rather than conventional: renaming it or handing it to a wrapper is refused as unsupported indirection, and removing the boundary is refused as a missing one. Both were falsified against this very file. ⚠️ ACC-0035 PASSED 2026-08-28 (TSK-0010), covering this component and CMP-0016 together: both selections come from the URL and nothing else, proven against a control URL rather than only against the happy path. ⚠️ COMPLETED 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0016. All four of its criteria now pass: ACC-0013 (derived stage), ACC-0014 (totals against an oracle), ACC-0015 (located parse failures) and ACC-0035 (URL-recoverable selection). ⚠️ TOTALS COME FROM THE PARSED SET FOR THAT REQUEST — never a file count, never a cached summary, never a displayed value. The split from TSK-0007 was made because this half fails SILENTLY, and it earned itself: a second instance of AST-0035's defect was found in the reader's own `artifactCount`, which had been counting files including unparsable ones since TSK-0005 and had simply never been rendered. ⚠️ LINT FINDINGS ARE SURFACED, NEVER RE-JUDGED (#47), and a static test forbids the panel calling `lintProject`, `loadArtifacts` or reclassifying a severity — a view that quietly disagreed with `npm run lint:plan` would be two answers to one question.
components.responsibility: Render `/`: the project's current stage derived from stage definitions and recorded attestations, navigation across all nine stages with each one's gate state, artifact counts, and lint findings. Report only counts it actually rendered.
components.title: Project view

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ AT MOST ONE STAGE DOCUMENT PER RENDER, because DEC-0020's per-request compilation cost is explicitly unmeasured and a view rendering several would multiply an unknown. ⚠️ NO CORRECTNESS-CRITICAL CLIENT STATE. Transient interface state is fine; anything a user must not lose is URL-encoded or persisted, because DEC-0022 reloads this page on every content change and every reconnection — at a moment the user did not choose and without telling them what went. ⚠️ OUTSIDE ITS BOUNDARY: it does not compile, read or write; it composes the components that do. ⚠️ BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0009. ACC-0016, ACC-0018 and ACC-0036 pass; ACC-0035 (URL-recoverable selection) stays `not-evaluated` and is TSK-0010's. ⚠️ THREE READS, THREE BOUNDARIES, and the independence was OBSERVED rather than argued: a successful response carried the resolved criteria alongside `data-vpw-loading="document"`, the document region still showing its own fallback in the same stream. ⚠️ THE REJECTION IS CAUGHT BEFORE IT ESCAPES, which is ACC-0036 and came from a measurement (AST-0039) rather than from caution. Uncaught, a refused document reaches the browser as HTTP 200 and an opaque digest — a blank region and a success status for something the compiler refused precisely. Caught, the region names the document by repository-relative path with a line and column, escapes the diagnostic as text, and leaves the exit criteria rendered beside it. ⚠️ THE REVIEW PANEL HAS NO WRITE CAPABILITY, deliberately and visibly. It names the artifact, its type, title and current status, and says the action is unavailable rather than omitting it: DEC-0021 reviews locking capabilities one at a time and TSK-0012 is where this one is examined.
components.responsibility: Render `/stage/[stageId]`: the stage's document through the restricted MDX compiler, its exit criteria with their recorded attestations, and the entry points for review actions. Hold no correctness-critical state in the client.
components.title: Stage view

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ THE HEARTBEAT IS A NAMED EVENT, NOT A COMMENT, and that correction came from AST-0036. A comment line is ignored by the client parser, so a comment keepalive fixes the bytes and not the visibility — the one consumer that needs to see it is the only one specified to ignore it. The skeleton's idle and dead streams are byte-identical (AST-0034), which is what REQ-0018's second clause forbids. ⚠️ RECONNECTION IS ITSELF A CHANGE HINT. Because events are hints and never deltas (#73), a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up — so no event buffer, no `id:` field and no `Last-Event-ID` handling are needed. This is the one place in the design where the contract removes work rather than adding it. ⚠️ A WATCHER FAILURE EMITS A VISIBLE SIGNAL OR CLOSES THE STREAM. Logging alone is forbidden: the operator is looking at a browser, and a logged failure with a live-looking page is the retained-workspace-reported-destroyed defect exactly. ⚠️ SERVER HALF BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0011. ACC-0028 and ACC-0031 pass. ACC-0029 (a stopped heartbeat produces a visibly stale page) and ACC-0030 (reconnect reloads and recovers a missed change) stay `not-evaluated` — they are about the CLIENT, and TSK-0017 owns it. ⚠️ IT IS A SERVICE, NOT AN IMPORT-TIME SIDE EFFECT. Nothing starts until the first subscription, chokidar is imported dynamically inside the factory, and `close()` is explicit so the service and its tests can end it deterministically. `next build` imports every route module to collect page data, and a watcher started at import would run during the build and outlive it. ⚠️ THE WATCHER IS SHARED AND THE SUBSCRIBERS ARE NOT. One tab closing clears its own timer and leaves every other page refreshing; the watcher closes when the last subscriber leaves. ⚠️ A FAILURE IS BROADCAST THEN THE STREAMS CLOSE, so a client can tell a dead watcher from a dropped connection. Logging alone would leave every open page looking healthy while nothing could ever refresh it — DEC-0022's rule, and the reason this is an event rather than a console line. ⚠️ CLIENT HALF BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0017 (EVD-0070). ACC-0029 and ACC-0030 STAY `not-evaluated`: no browser was available, and both are about what a page does, not about what the logic would do. The logic behind them is tested; the behaviour is not observed, and marking them would claim a measurement nobody took. ⚠️ IT IS THE APPLICATION'S ONLY CLIENT COMPONENT, and it holds nothing a reload would lose — DEC-0023's rule as corrected. `location.reload()` rather than an assignment, so the URL and with it both selections survive every refresh this component causes. ⚠️ STATE IS TEXT FIRST, icon second, colour last. AST-0034 measured an idle stream and a dead one as byte-identical: this indicator is the only thing between the operator and a page that looks fine while nothing can refresh it, so it must not depend on colour to be read. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: an earlier note here said `close()` was 'explicit for TSK-0013's launcher to own'. It is not and cannot be — the launcher is a parent process and this service is an in-process singleton inside its child. `close()` is a SERVICE AND TEST lifecycle operation: the service calls it when its last subscriber leaves, and tests call it to end a stream deterministically. What the launcher contributes is terminating the child, after which process teardown releases anything still open. ⚠️ ACC-0029 AND ACC-0030 EVALUATED 2026-08-29 IN A REAL BROWSER (EVD-0075); both pass, and the first run of that evaluation FAILED and found a defect that made this component inert in every shipped page. `timers = { setTimeout, clearTimeout }` throws `Illegal invocation` in a browser (AST-0040); the watchdog never armed, and the indicator reported a healthy stream forever. Thirteen unit tests passed throughout, because every one of them injected timers and none called the default. ⚠️ `test/stream-watchdog.test.mjs` NOW CALLS THE DEFAULT with `globalThis.setTimeout` wrapped in the same brand check a browser applies, so the defect is catchable in Node from now on. It was falsified against the original code before being trusted.
components.responsibility: Keep every open view current: watch the content root, emit a named heartbeat event carrying data at a fixed interval, deliver change notifications as hints, and run the client watchdog that renders a visibly disconnected state when a heartbeat does not arrive. On reconnection, reload.
components.title: Change stream

components.notes: ⚠️ EVERY FIELD IS THERE TO DEFEAT A SPECIFIC LOOKALIKE. The run id defeats a previous Kiln process still holding the port; the project id defeats a Kiln serving a different project; the service name and protocol defeat an unrelated application that happens to return JSON.
components.responsibility: Answer the supervisor's readiness question with an identity rather than a status: the service name, a versioned health protocol, the ephemeral run identifier of this invocation, the non-secret stable project identifier, and the build version — and nothing else, in particular no absolute path, no credential, and no session or planning content.
components.title: Run-identity health endpoint

note: Generated as a query over the task graph, grouped by `task.role` (#19). Nothing here is authored: re-running the handoff recomputes it, so a slice cannot drift from the plan. `tasks` is work REMAINING; `accepted` is work already finished, listed so nobody repeats it. Both statuses are derived from acceptance criteria, never stored.

requirements.rationale: REQ-0002 requires current project state to be inspectable at any time, and stage position is the coarsest form of that state. Deriving it rather than storing it follows #16: stage status is derived from artifacts, never persisted alongside them.
requirements.statement: The application shows which stage the project is in, derived from the stage definitions and the recorded attestations rather than from a stored status value.
requirements.title: The application displays the project's current stage

requirements.rationale: Stage documents are the narrative half of the plan and are agent-authored. Rendering them is the point of choosing MDX; bounding what they may execute is what keeps content from becoming application code.
requirements.statement: The application renders the MDX stage document for a selected stage, and a document referencing a component outside the permitted set does not execute arbitrary code.
requirements.title: The application renders a stage document authored in MDX

requirements.rationale: The agent and the operator write the same files (#15), so a view that only refreshes on reload shows state that has already moved. The second clause is the harder half: a silently dead stream renders stale content that looks live.
requirements.statement: When a file under the content root is changed by something other than the application, the application's view updates without the operator reloading the page, and a dropped update stream is visibly distinguishable from an idle one.
requirements.title: The application reflects external content changes without a manual reload

requirements.rationale: #88 forbids authoring content by any route but a typed operation, and #78 plus #72 make the write safe against the agent writing concurrently. A second write path in the app would be a second protocol against the same files.
requirements.statement: A review-status change made in the application is written by the existing typed operation — lock, fresh read inside the lock, atomic write — and the application contains no other write path into content.
requirements.title: The application performs review-status updates through the existing typed write path

requirements.notes: ⚠️ THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS TESTABLE, and it should be written before the check: stand up an unrelated healthy HTTP server on the port and require launch to refuse. A readiness check without that control has never been shown to check anything.
requirements.rationale: The current launcher polls `GET /` on the configured port and treats any HTTP response as ready. An unrelated service already listening on port 3000 therefore satisfies it, and the operator is told the browser workspace is up while looking at somebody else's application. The same shape recurs across the layer: an extension that loaded, a model that replied, a session that resumed — each is only evidence if something distinguishes it from a lookalike.
requirements.statement: Before reporting a component ready, the system must confirm the identity of whatever responded: that the HTTP service answering the port is the process this invocation started and is serving this project, that the loaded package is the one it installed, and that the model answering is the one recorded. A response that merely arrives, from an unidentified source, is not readiness and must not be reported as such.
requirements.title: A readiness claim names what answered
